code_label: Hybrid cloud quantum platforms exist
text_span: There are several companies now offering commercial-grade Hybrid Classical-Quantum computers that can be accessed via the Cloud
rationale: States the practical context motivating the paper's hybrid computing framing.

code_label: Classical computers can emulate hybrid workflow
text_span: This project essentially codes generated for two previous XSEDE grants
rationale: Describes the implementation choice of using classical computers to run the hybrid workflow.

code_label: Classical-only implementation of hybrid quantum features
text_span: These codes run on Classical computers, defining a Hybrid Classical-Quantum solely on a Classical computer.
rationale: Explicitly states the methodological decision to simulate hybrid classical-quantum behavior on classical hardware.

code_label: Quantum money motivates financial modeling
text_span: For over two-score years, there have been occasional papers proposing Quantum Money (QM)
rationale: Introduces the financial-quantum motivation for the study.

code_label: Paper focuses on options on quantum money
text_span: This paper does not address these problems in defining QM. Instead, this papaer addresses how options on such QM can be calculated.
rationale: Clarifies the paper's scope and what it does and does not address.

code_label: Need for numerical option methods
text_span: American options, that can be exercised before maturation, prominent in today’s markets, and these require numerical algorithms.
rationale: States why numerical methods are needed in the financial setting.

code_label: Non-Gaussian market distributions require fitting
text_span: probability distributions of prices in real markets will not generally be simple Gaussian or log-normal distributions that yield closed form options solutions.
rationale: Identifies a modeling challenge that motivates the paper's fitting approach.

code_label: SMNI background from neocortical modeling
text_span: Previous papers since 1981 have have calculated properties of a model of neocortex, Statistical Mechanics of Neocortical Interactions (SMNI), to fit/describe many experimental data
rationale: Provides the prior modeling lineage that the paper builds on.

code_label: Quantum wave-packet mechanism in SMNI
text_span: using a model of quantum wave-packets composed of a specific class of Ca! ions that are (re-)generated at tripartite neuron-astrocyte-neuron sites
rationale: Describes the quantum-inspired mechanism referenced as prior work.

code_label: Path-integral codes handle random shocks
text_span: The codes PATHTREE/qPATHTREE and PATHINT/qPATHINT can include random shocks in the evolution of a short-time probability distribution over thousands of foldings
rationale: States a key capability of the computational codes used in the project.

code_label: PATHINT generalized to N dimensions
text_span: This was generalized to PATHINT to an N-dimentional code.
rationale: Identifies a methodological extension of the path-integral code.

code_label: Quantum generalization of path-integral code
text_span: The 1-D PATHINT code was generalized by the author to N dimensions. A quantum generalization also was made to the code
rationale: States the development of the quantum version of the algorithm.

code_label: qPATHINT changes variables to complex form
text_span: changing all variables and functions to complex variables
rationale: Specifies a concrete implementation change for the quantum code.

code_label: Monte Carlo not convenient for serial shocks
text_span: This project, however, concerns time-sequential serial random shocks, which are not conveniently treated with Monte-Carlo/importance-sampling algorithms.
rationale: States a limitation of Monte Carlo methods for the problem addressed.

code_label: Hybrid calculation uses classical fitting and quantum propagation
text_span: Above considerations define fitting a volatility of volatility options model with Classical algorithms, with qPATHINT numerically calculating the Quantum path-integrals at each time between epochs.
rationale: Summarizes the hybrid workflow combining classical fitting and quantum path-integral calculation.

code_label: Epoch reset after decoherence
text_span: At the beginning of each epoch, time is reset (t=0) since the wave-function is decohered (“collapsed”) by a prior American stop-measurement
rationale: Describes the temporal structure and measurement assumption used in the model.

code_label: Two-factor model includes stochastic volatility
text_span: The two-factor model includes stochastic volatility σ of the underlying S
rationale: Defines the main two-factor financial model used in the paper.

code_label: Piecewise noise function for underlying price
rationale: Specifies the piecewise functional form used in the stochastic differential equation.

code_label: Black-Scholes limit used to avoid negative prices
text_span: The Black-Scholes form F= S inside S < S' is used so that no negative prices arise since the distribution is excluded from S < 0.
rationale: Explains a modeling choice and its intended numerical safeguard.

code_label: Alternative smooth cutoff forms were tested
text_span: Some experimentation was performed with alternative functional forms, e.g., appling smooth cutoffs across the above three regions of S.
rationale: Reports an exploratory methodological variation.

code_label: Central region most sensitive in fits
text_span: Fits were most sensitive to the data when the central region was simply S2 using F above.
rationale: Reports an empirical observation about fit sensitivity.

code_label: Mesh depends on volatility in two-factor model
text_span: the mesh of S would depend on σ and cause some problems in any PATHINT grid to be developed in S-σ.
rationale: Identifies a numerical difficulty in extending the grid to two factors.

code_label: Diagonal mesh tiling proposed for multivariate systems
text_span: Another method, is to develop a tiling of diagonal meshes for each factor i that often are suitable for off-diagonal regions in an n-factor system
rationale: Describes a proposed numerical strategy for multivariate diffusion problems.

code_label: Minimal mesh chosen in important regions
text_span: giving a minimal mesh ΔM'i in regions of the Lagrangian with most important contributions to the distribution.
rationale: States the mesh-selection principle used in the algorithm.

code_label: ATM scaling preserves Greeks
text_span: After the at-the-money BPV are scaled to be equivalent, there is not a very large change in the one-factor ATM Greeks.
rationale: Reports an observed effect of the scaling choice on option sensitivities.

code_label: Limited volatility equation range works well
text_span: This works well, taking the σ equation with a limited range of influence in the calculations.
rationale: States a positive assessment of the chosen numerical treatment.

code_label: Shocks affect higher-order Greeks strongly
text_span: Shocks affect Greeks with “p” severely, where “p” denotes additional orders of derivatives.
rationale: Reports sensitivity of higher-order derivatives to shocks.

code_label: VegapPI is highly sensitive
text_span: E.g., VegapPI (second derivative of Υ with respect to volatility) is very sensitive to shocks in this drift.
rationale: Gives a specific example of sensitivity in the model outputs.

code_label: Current project fits volatility of volatility options
text_span: ASA is used to fit volatility of volatility options over short-time conditional probability distributions
rationale: States the immediate analytical goal of the project.

code_label: Quantum money is the target market context
text_span: but now these forms are based on Quantum, instead of Classical, money.
rationale: Specifies the quantum-financial context of the fitted model.

code_label: Scaling benchmark for one-dimensional system
text_span: SMNI estimates were made on XSEDE.org’s Expanse using ‘gcc -O3‘, and for the one-dimensional system.
rationale: Provides the benchmark environment and system size for performance estimates.

code_label: One-dimensional runtime reported
text_span: This runs in 0.002s, giving 0.0002s/qIteraction.
rationale: Reports a concrete runtime measurement.

code_label: Higher dimensions grow rapidly in kernel size
rationale: Illustrates the rapid scaling of the kernel size with dimension.

code_label: Two-dimensional problem much more expensive
text_span: The 2-D problem takes on the order of 200 times the 1-D problem.
rationale: Summarizes the reported scaling cost increase.

code_label: Parameter fitting recommended for higher dimensions
text_span: When the length of time is an issue, e.g., for dimensions > 2, fits of drifts and covariance matrices to parameterized forms is a very good option
rationale: Offers a recommended approach for handling scaling challenges.

code_label: Pilot studies justify kernel-based quantum path integrals
text_span: Pilot studies give rationales for developing this particular kernel-based quantum path-integral algorithm.
rationale: States the concluding justification for the algorithm.

code_label: Serial random shocks are a target use case
text_span: This can study serial random shocks that occur in many real systems.
rationale: Summarizes the intended applicability of the method.

code_label: qPATHINT applicable to many quantum systems
text_span: qPATHINT can be used for many quantum systems which are becoming increasingly important.
rationale: Indicates broader future applicability of the quantum algorithm.
